authorization: User explicitly requested more creative screen composition unconstrained by the current game layout. Existing action semantics remain; control positions, grouping, category presentation and inventory browsing are design proposals.
source_reference_role: Approved restaurant WORLD art only; no previous editor screenshot was supplied, and no exact current UI layout was retained.
shared_principles: One primary Live action with quieter Shop
Composed restaurant with a clear central focus and placement aisle
Rotate and Return grouped in one contextual capsule attached to the selected object
One editing drawer with integrated category navigation and large inventory previews
Material identity and controlled typography shared across interactive and passive surfaces

steps.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate one original, fully art-directed portrait mobile game screen, approximately 1080 x 2340, full bleed, no phone hardware or presentation margins.
The game is a cozy sushi restaurant builder for Android. It is paused in furniture editing mode. The player selects, moves, rotates and returns placed furniture and drags owned inventory into the room. Keep the restaurant appealing and playable.
The input image is a WORLD ART reference only: chunky, low-poly, matte sushi furniture, chubby people, warm lighting and a square tiled restaurant. Do not copy its UI or exact layout. This is a NEW screen composition, not a reskin. Create a convincing designed restaurant with a central continuous U-shaped charcoal conveyor, quiet clay rails and hinoki wood legs, several backless stools, smiling chubby chefs and seated customers, two lush corner plants, a four-cell-wide entrance with a cloth noren, warm lanterns and calm cream square floor. Use a screen-aligned square top/front oblique grid, all rows and columns parallel to screen axes, no diamond/isometric grid. Give the scene a coherent silhouette and clear walking aisle. Show seven tiles across. Furniture has broad readable facets, shadowed lower forms and soft grounding. Show a selected unoccupied stool on a restrained sage tile footprint. All people and in-world furniture belong to the same visual scale.
We are testing a more commercial art direction with creative freedom over every HUD position and panel composition. UI has confident typography, deliberate spacing, one clear action hierarchy, crafted icon silhouettes and a restaurant-specific material identity. Main scene remains the hero, about the middle 65 percent. Make one coherent editing drawer in the lower quarter, not scattered equal-weight panels around all edges. The selected stool has a small legible connected capsule with labeled "Rotate" and "Return" actions. No enormous standalone floating tools.
Required functionality visible: coin count "1,240", compact "Shop", primary "Live" to return to service, inventory categories "People", "Layout", "Floor" with Layout selected, stock previews for "Conveyor" with "6", "Wood stool" with "4", and "Plant" with "2". Recompose them freely as directed below. Draw LARGE clearly recognizable furniture cutouts in the drawer, with small stock badges and short readable names, no visually heavy individual picture frames. A partial next item at the right edge may suggest browsing. No page counters, plus/minus, Save, Done, Undo, extra currencies, hearts, energy, tasks or settings. Include only these useful controls; no game name, marketing title, watermark, design annotations, fake Japanese lettering or decorative sushi scattered on UI.
Typography: contemporary friendly rounded sans with open counters, clean careful kerning, a bold expressive heading and quieter functional labels. No outlined bubble text. Icons use a consistent family of clean hand-painted silhouettes with restrained relief, not generic app line icons and not giant gold clipart. Exceptionally readable on a phone.

DIRECTION A — CEDAR WORKSHOP, warm and crafted.
The interface takes inspiration from a beautiful sushi bar's cedar counter and paper menu: pale warm rice-paper cream, rich espresso ink, softly illustrated honey-cedar edges, restrained jade green. Use real art direction and beautiful value grouping, not rustic fantasy planks. A few carefully drawn wood strokes, slim material edges, an inset cream sheet and short ambient shadows; no metallic bolts or stacked bevels.
Top composition: an almost invisible ink-and-cream coin cluster at upper left; at upper right a deliberately prominent jade "Live" capsule with a small play arrow. Small quiet "Editing" mode label between them. Plenty of space between the top controls and the entrance art.
Bottom drawer: an elegant wide CEDAR COUNTER lip supports one light paper inventory sheet. Its material silhouette is sculpted as one piece, with softly swept upper corners and a small off-center folded-paper detail. The top line is an integrated category strip with "People", "Layout", "Floor"; active Layout is an ivory raised paper tab with a narrow jade accent. Put a compact basket + "Shop" at the far right of this same strip, aligned with it, not floating in the scene.
Below, three furniture previews sit on generous pale paper mats, item names in strong espresso type and small jade stock seals. The objects, labels and stock badges align to one invisible baseline grid. Leave cream breathing room. No double-framed cards.
The room has welcoming warm morning light, walnut/cedar furniture and sage clothing/cushions. UI is beautifully drawn 2D material illustration over a dimensional toy-like world. Warm, trustworthy, tactile, expertly restrained, with the visual completeness and coherence of a polished shipped mobile management game.

Edit this complete Cedar Workshop restaurant-editor concept locally, preserving its full-screen composition, warm art direction, all text, world and character arrangement, tabs, stock counts and selected stool.
Correct three UI details:
1. Replace the small trash-can icon above the word "Return" with a clearly illustrated open storage box with a down/inward arrow. Return means retain this object in inventory; it must never imply deletion.
2. The inventory object above "Conveyor" currently shows an entire U-shaped restaurant belt. Replace just that one inventory illustration with a single straight one-cell conveyor module with charcoal belt top, warm muted-clay rails and wooden legs, matching the room's material family. Keep the same name and stock "6".
3. Make the bottom "Shop" button a quiet warm ivory paper/ceramic secondary control with espresso basket and text, a slim drawn edge and short soft shadow. Only the top "Live" button retains saturated jade green as the primary action.
Keep every other detail and label unchanged. One full portrait screen, no crop, no device frame or notes.

DIRECTION B — INDIGO NOREN & PORCELAIN, bold and distinctive.
Create a confident Japanese neighborhood sushi-house visual identity: warm ivory porcelain, deep blue-black indigo, one precise vermilion accent, wasabi green supporting tones. Wood is the world and a small UI structural accent, not the surface of every button. Modern and playful, beautifully illustrated game UI rather than a minimalist web app.
The distinctive bottom editing drawer feels like a cream porcelain serving tray resting on a slim dark cedar base. A broad but shallow deep-indigo NORÉN CLOTH strip forms its upper edge, with two subtle cloth notches and quiet seam detail. Categories "People", "Layout", "Floor" are arranged horizontally in this indigo strip, cream typography, Layout marked by a small vermilion seal and brighter text. A compact cream basket icon + "Shop" sits at the strip's right edge. Below, furniture cutouts are displayed like carefully arranged products on warm ivory with faint indigo mats, bold navy labels and tiny round stock seals. No separate framed inventory cards.
Top composition: small coin "1,240" cluster left, tiny ink "Editing" state label nearby, and one strong VERMILION "Live" pill at top right. Refined ivory ceramic edges and soft short shadows. All controls align with clear margins, no broad header blocking the room.
Selected stool: gentle mint occupied-cell tint and precise indigo corner marks. One thin ivory contextual capsule just above the stool contains Rotate and Return separated by an ink hairline; icons and labels are compact, completely legible.
The restaurant is a coherent warm evening cutaway, with indigo entrance curtain, soft amber lantern light, pale cream floor, warm cedar and subdued clay belt trim. Lively food and character colors draw attention inside an otherwise disciplined palette. Thin confident ink rims on UI, no outlines on broad low-poly scene facets. Keep highlights crisp but sparse, broad calm values, asymmetric visual interest with excellent balance. Boutique and charming, commercially finished, not generic orange wooden game-kit art.

Functional icon precision: the Return action means keep the object in inventory, so use an open storage box with an inward arrow, NEVER a trash/delete icon. Conveyor inventory artwork is one straight single-cell conveyor MODULE, not a whole U-shaped route. Shop is a quiet secondary ivory control, while Live is the only high-saturation filled primary action. Keep stock badges near each object and show their readable numbers.

Edit this complete Indigo Noren & Porcelain portrait restaurant-editor concept. Keep the full composition, world art, people, restaurant arrangement, contextual tools, inventory items, all text and screen proportions unchanged. Make just these precise interface refinements:
1. In the dark indigo category rail, replace the little vermilion icon above/next to "Layout" that resembles a torii gate with a recognizable cream backless STOOL / furniture pictogram inside the same small vermilion rounded square. Do not use a gate or building icon. Keep the active underline.
2. Change the THREE red stock circles containing "6", "4" and "2" to warm IVORY circles with clear dark INDIGO numerals and a fine indigo rim. Keep their sizes and positions. Reserve strong vermilion for the top Live action and the tiny active-category accent. Stock is neutral inventory information.
3. Make the existing cream Shop control slightly more pill-shaped and give it a little breathing room from the three indigo category tabs, so it reads as a separate secondary action. Preserve its basket icon and "Shop" label and overall position. Do not add any new panel or controls.
All other details stay unchanged. Retain crisp readable typography, coherent ceramic/ink/cloth material language, soft shallow shadows, matte furniture and the appealing complete restaurant composition. Output the same ONE full portrait screen without annotations, no crop or device frame.

limits: Static composition/UI direction studies, not native captures or finished reusable assets.
Generated world composition, projection, new props and character renders remain illustrative and do not supersede approved native sprite/projection contracts.
No runtime layout change, atlas extraction, APK publication, ticket closure or user acceptance is implied.
All final generated raster output is preserved without resizing or postprocessing; dynamic labels remain baked into these mockups only.

approval.scope: Issue #12 and the shared family for every future UI ticket. User authorized creative UI composition beyond the old layout; editor behavior and pause/save contracts remain.
supersedes: two Layout inventory items per page
